```{r}
#| echo: false
data(Theoph)
# `Theoph$Subject` is the real column name in base R's built-in Theoph
# dataset -- the variable names below are this fragment's own choice of
# words for that data, not part of the dataset's schema.
participants <- split(Theoph, Theoph$Subject)
halflives <- sapply(participants, function(d) {
  d <- d[order(d$Time), ]
  peak_idx <- which.max(d$conc)
  terminal <- d[d$Time > d$Time[peak_idx] & d$conc > 0, ]
  fit <- lm(log(conc) ~ Time, data = terminal)
  k <- -coef(fit)[["Time"]]
  log(2) / k
})
mean_half_life <- round(mean(halflives), 1)
```

Fitting a simple log-linear elimination model to each of the 12
participants' terminal-phase concentrations in the built-in `Theoph`
dataset gives a population mean elimination half-life of
**`r mean_half_life` hours** -- consistent with theophylline's
established ~8-hour half-life.

This is a simple per-participant regression for illustration, not a
population PK model.
